gold: Strangulated sciatic hernia with intestinal perforation
e7_s4_rationale: The presence of a palpable, painful mass in the left buttock area, radiating pain down the back of the left thigh, and imaging studies showing incarcerated bowel loops beneath the left gluteal muscles and herniation through the left sciatic foramen containing a small bowel loop are consistent with a sciatic hernia.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Strangulated femoral hernia
e7_s4_rejected.why: The location of the hernia is not consistent with a femoral hernia, which typically occurs below the inguinal ligament and not in the buttock area.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Incercerated Spigelian hernia
e7_s4_rejected.why: Spigelian hernias occur through the spigelian fascia, which is located between the rectus abdominis muscle and the semilunar line, not in the buttock area.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Obstructed inguinal hernia
e7_s4_rejected.why: The location of the hernia and the radiating pain are not consistent with an inguinal hernia, which typically occurs in the groin area.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Internal hernia
e7_s4_rejected.why: Internal hernias occur within the abdominal cavity and do not typically present with a palpable mass in the buttock area.
